result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy values verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no scheme stripping, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches `lower(host) = uri.host` (bare hostname). The old deleted `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` used `(URI(h).host rescue nil) || h` which stripped schemes, and the deleted specs confirm `http://eviltrout.com` in settings worked. So a migrated host with a scheme prefix never matches, breaking existing embeds — a real correctness/data-migration bug.

judged_text: The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting entries verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation scheme/path stripping, so entries like `http://eviltrout.com` — which the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly accepted (it stripped the scheme before comparing, per the specs this diff deletes) — are stored with the `http://` prefix intact. After upgrade, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the bare referer host from `uri.host`, so a migrated `http://example.com` row never matches and every embed request from that host returns InvalidAccess — existing embeds break silently across the site with no error and no migration warning.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` inserts legacy hosts via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without running `EmbeddableHost` validations/callbacks. The `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` is what strips `http(s)://` and paths, but it won’t run for these inserts. Meanwhile `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the request URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against the bare `uri.host`. If a migrated row is stored as `http://eviltrout.com`, it will not match `eviltrout.com`, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embeds will be rejected post-upgrade for those legacy entries.
